messages:
raj: quick thread — we need to settle on an internal API strategy for the new inference router. two options on the table: 1) content-negotiation at the edge (Accept: application/x-proto or application/json) + gateway translator, or 2) gRPC-native client calls internally and only JSON REST at the public edge. thinking about telemetry signal fidelity, quota enforcement, and rollout UX. what do folks prefer?
maria: my +1 is for gRPC internally. easier to keep typed contracts and avoids repeated translation overhead. also telemetry -> spans/metrics map cleaner.
han: i'm worried about client ergonomics if we go pure gRPC. a lot of internal teams are web-first and will want simple REST hooks. can we do gRPC internal + light JSON shim at the edge?
simon: that's the compromise we've used before. edge converts JSON -> protobuf for internal calls. downside: hard to get per-token telemetry right because translation masks original shape unless we emit extra attrs.
devon: telemetry pain: if gateway translates, we lose schema-level metrics unless gateway annotates traces with original fields. we could add trace tags like `x.infer.model` and `x.infer.req_shape` before translation. cheap but fragile.
raj: proposal: gRPC internal, edge shim for web clients, and an explicit header to opt into raw gRPC routing for teams that can handle it. rollout plan: start with 10% of traffic routed as gRPC-internal for a subset of tenants. metrics to watch: request.latency, tokens.generated, translate.time, error.rate, quota.denied.
maria: +1. for quotas we should enforce at the gateway boundary only (prevent overage), but also have internal per-model quotas enforced by runtime for fairness. the gateway quota is the billing gate, runtime quota is fairness guard.
han: that makes sense. For console UX, can we show both quota counters side-by-side? billing vs fairness? product asked for single view.
simon: doable — console can surface both but label clearly. also add an annotation when translation is happening. might help debugging.
devon: small config snippet for rollout I think we can use:

```
route:
  match: /v1/infer
  method: POST
  canary:
    header: x-canary
    percent: 10
  backend_preference: [grpc_internal, grpc_shim]
  telemetry: emit_translate_time: true
```

raj: perfect. For telemetry namespacing: prefer `router.translate_ms` and `router.backend_choice` tags. keep stable names for dashboards.
maria: also add `router.client_type` (web, grpc_native, sdk). helps in dashboards + cost allocation.
han: about schema evolution: if we keep protos internal we can evolve with minor fields additive. gateway translation should fail fast when unknown required fields appear. don't let silent drops happen.
simon: agree. mention in rollout docs: `translation-strict: true` default for canary, relaxed after 2 weeks of zero breaks.
devon: infra-bot ping: starting canary flow will create a new route version. @deploy-bot can we get an infra job to apply config at 10%?
deploy-bot: deploy job queued: infra/edge/route-update v2026.03-canary-001. ETA ~20m. logs will emit under `infra.deploys`. :rocket: 
raj: thanks. action items: han -> update console mock for dual-quota view; simon -> add trace tags and metric names; devon -> create rollout playbook with abort thresholds; maria -> sign off on quota policy doc. We'll reconvene after canary smoke. :thumbsup:
